root_causes.description: product-catalog serves requests with server-side p99 latency pinned at the ~10000ms ceiling throughout the incident window, while its error rate, CPU usage, memory usage and pod restart count all remain at normal baselines. As a leaf dependency of frontend, checkout and recommendation, this latency propagates up the call graph, driving all callers to ~10s p99.

evidence.expected_baseline: error_rate < 0.01; no HTTP abort present, ruling out http_abort
< 0.1 cores; confirms no CPU saturation, ruling out cpu_stress
~24 MB steady; no memory pressure, ruling out memory_stress
frontend p99 < few hundred ms; inflated by product-catalog dependency
recommendation p99 < few hundred ms; inflated by product-catalog dependency
checkout p99 < few hundred ms; inflated by product-catalog dependency
no errors; consistent with latency injection rather than failing calls

evidence.query_or_id: Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource (count=1)
evidence.observed_value: only benign controller update events for product-catalog pods; no OOMKilled/BackOff/FailedMount
evidence.expected_baseline: no crash/restart events; rules out pod_crash

remediation_steps: Confirm and disable the injected latency fault on product-catalog (flagd fault-injection flag or tc netem / latency sidecar for the seed42 scenario) and roll it back.
Inspect product-catalog request handling for artificial sleeps or downstream I/O stalls to verify the ~10s delay is injected rather than a genuine backend slowdown.
Restart/roll the product-catalog deployment to clear any stuck latency condition, then confirm product-catalog p99 returns below ~100ms and that frontend, checkout and recommendation p99 recover.
